Browser journeys: 16/16 passed.
Requirements: 3 demonstrated, 0 failed, 4 unverified.

criteria.requirement: The tool must deploy collaborative departmental agents (Engineering Agent, Weapons Agent, Combat Systems Agent, etc.) that negotiate drill schedules against shared constraints: ship operational windows, qualified personnel rosters (e.g., Fire Party Leader, EOOW, TAO), and fatigue policies. The multi-agent solver identifies personnel collisions, proposes alternate schedule allocations, and ensures all SFTRM-mandated training periodicities are satisfied.
criteria.detail: The slice demonstrates deterministic feasibility for synthetic departmental requests only. No collaborating agents, authoritative fatigue policy, SFTRM rules or completion history are supplied. Full source requirement remains unverified.

criteria.requirement: No personnel or shared-resource double booking.
criteria.detail: Every complete proposal has zero overlapping interval pairs sharing personnel or an exclusive resource. In the planned two-request example, Damage Control occupies Monday 09:00–10:00 UTC and Engineering moves from 09:00 to 10:30–11:30 UTC; both use Alex and Room A without overlap. Proposal edits invalidate prior review. — demonstrated by resolve-collision, review-revision at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: Honor availability, qualifications, rest and duty budgets.
criteria.detail: Within explicit synthetic inputs, every assigned interval is contained in a ship operating window and every assigned person availability window, all required qualifications are covered by assigned people, every same-person pair satisfies supplied rest and total horizon duty does not exceed budget. Missing FPL, availability ending at minute 600, rest 31 and duty budget 119 prevent the two-request proposal; restoring availability to 1020, rest 30 and budget 120 yields both requests and exactly 120 duty minutes. These are demonstration values, not approved policy. — demonstrated by recover-qualification, recover-availability, recover-fatigue at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: Distinguish infeasible input from exhausted search.
criteria.detail: An exhaustive search of the impossible two-request candidate set reports Infeasible: no complete schedule within supplied candidates. A one-node budget reports Search limit reached: feasibility is unknown. Neither exposes an approvable partial proposal. Invalid duration is rejected as validation, separate from either solver result. Correcting inputs or increasing budget recovers a complete feasible proposal. — demonstrated by recover-exhaustion, recover-impossible, recover-invalid at both viewport sizes.

Owner-approved periodicity rules, applicability and completion history are missing. Two explicit synthetic occurrences do not establish recurrence completeness or SFTRM compliance. No mandatory-compliance indicator will be shown.

criteria.requirement: Have an operator accept the proposed schedule.
criteria.detail: Local revision-bound acceptance and edit protection are demonstrated, but automated interaction cannot establish actual operator acceptance. No authorized operator or human acceptance evidence is supplied. Hard constraints are never relaxed automatically.

criteria.requirement: An interactive weekly schedule board showing automated conflict resolution across departments with one-click schedule optimization and personnel loading heatmaps.
criteria.detail: The prototype supplies a weekly editable board, conflict comparison, one-action feasible allocation and numeric heatmap. Bounded first-feasible search has no optimization objective or optimality guarantee; the full deliverable remains unverified pending owner definition and implementation of optimization.
